target_customer: Online marketplaces and e-commerce apps that want better search, feed ranking and native ads
problem: Marketplaces lack in-house ranking and ads systems like those built at Google and Pinterest, so relevance and revenue lag.
business_model: B2B SaaS and revenue share on marketplace ads
product_category: Marketplace search, ads and feed ranking infrastructure

founders.name: Andrew Yates
founders.background_notes: Described as a former Pinterest engineer manager, other sources mention Facebook and Google ad systems; unclear.

founders.name: Dan Hill
founders.background_notes: About 18 years building ad systems per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Building large scale ranking, ads auction and measurement systems needs deep machine learning and ads infrastructure experience.

defensibility.rationale: Deep integration into marketplace search and ads and learning from behavior data, though search vendors could build similar features.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Search vendors added ads and ranking later; Dropbox acquired Promoted.ai in 2025.

market_need_then: Marketplaces wanted ad revenue and better relevance, and customers such as Upwork integrated its search and native ads engine by 2024.

branding.community_and_virality: Founder interviews and a Sacra research series, but no community or merch evidence.

brand_strength.rationale: Known in marketplace and ads circles via interviews, but generic with no distinct asset.

outcome_analysis: Promoted was started by ex Pinterest and Google ads engineers, raised roughly $8M across two seed rounds, and landed marketplace customers including Eventbrite, Upwork and Outschool. It was acquired by Dropbox in April or May 2025; the price was not disclosed, so the strength of the exit is unknown. Deep founder expertise in ads systems and a clear customer segment drove the traction.
notes: Website promoted.ai could not be resolved from the session. Sources disagree on lead investors and on totals ($8M to $10M). Acquisition date differs between MergerLinks (April 24 2025) and Signalbase (May 10 2025); the YC page cites April 30 2025. The founder Andrew Yates is not on the YC page, which lists only Dan Hill, so the founders list relies on press. Competitor search returned only current vendor pages, so the list is empty.
